(4) A Trillion Operations for 16'968 ÷ 404?

CPU Computation LLM Inference
Elapsed time a few nanoseconds ~0.1–2 seconds
Computation one integer division ~1011–1013 FLOPs
Energy ~pJ–nJ ~1–100 J
Correctness exact not guaranteed
  • CPU: One deterministic instruction
  • LLM: Trillions of operations for probabilistic inference
  • The LLM might still get the answer wrong


AI Engineering is Growing Up Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(5) AI All The Things?

Perfect Vision Current Reality
  • One agent, one model, all tasks
  • Always gets the right answer
  • Autonomous, self-directing, self-correcting
  • No human engineering required
  • Just describe what you want and trust it
  • Same prompt returns different answers
  • Behavior drift on model updates
  • Most business logic is deterministic
  • AI earns its keep on judgment tasks
  • Reliability = clean cuts between the two


AI Engineering is Growing Up Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(6) AI at Design Time! AI at Runtime?

AI at Design Time AI at Runtime
  • Recognizes patterns
  • Writes the code
  • You review and ship
  • Runs deterministically forever after
  • Use it aggressively
  • Great tool for genuine judgment tasks
  • Great tool for unstructured input at scale
  • Real value where no non-AI option exists
  • Costly per call — budget deliberately
  • Handle with care

(8) The Boundary Has a History

Before Machine Learning Machine Learning Generative AI
  • No boundary at all
  • Everything is code
  • If code could not do it, you did not build it
  • Boundary appears
  • Probabilistic components are possible but expensive
  • Keep ML parts small and deliberate
  • Cost collapses
  • Boundary moves a long way, fast
  • Not clear where and why and how to manage
  • The boundary should sit where constraints put it
  • Generative AI changed the price, not the principle


Where the Line Runs Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(9) It's Software Architecture

  • Macro architecture: domains and the interfaces between them remain unchanged
  • The GenAI / non-GenAI line is not a domain boundary
  • It runs inside every domain: judgment work and deterministic work co-exist
  • Micro architecture: where that line sits, and which mechanism crosses it
  • The line may move because of new processes and workflows and insights

(11) Two Kinds of Component, Two Kinds of Contract

Deterministic Probabilistic
  • Same input, same output
  • Tested exhaustively (within reason)
  • Composes predictably
  • Behavior is and remains stable
  • Failure is exceptional
  • Same input, a distribution of outputs
  • Evaluated statistically and at runtime
  • Adapts to what it is given
  • Behavior varies and may change at runtime
  • Variation is expected


Two Realms Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(12) What Each Realm Costs You

Probabilistic Deterministic
  • You delegate judgment
  • You give up repeatability
  • The uncertainty is in the answer
  • Managed with evals: statistical, after the fact
  • You specify everything yourself
  • You give up adaptability
  • The uncertainty is in the cases you did not anticipate
  • Managed with tests: exhaustive, before the fact

What to Use When Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(15) Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Use for Not for
  • Letting an LLM reach any external capability
  • Exposing your APIs, databases, workflows as tools
  • Deterministic operations the LLM should invoke on demand
  • The default answer for how do I connect the LLM to X?
  • Packaging prompt patterns (that's skills)
  • Complex multi-step business processes (wrap a workflow instead)
  • Delegating whole reasoning tasks (that's sub-agents)
  • Anywhere you need guaranteed invocation (LLM decides when to call)
  • Bottom line: MCP ⇏ guaranteed invocation


What to Use When Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(16) Skills

Use for Not for
  • Packaging a prompt pattern you keep re-typing
  • Sharing a way of working across sessions and projects
  • Loading context (style guides, docs) on demand
  • Composing MCP tool usage into a reusable recipe
  • Reliable business processes (workflows do this better)
  • Behavior that must run identically each time
  • Anything that needs versioning or auditability
  • Delegating to a different model (sub-agents)
  • Bottom line: Skills ⇏ reproducibility

(18) The Line Moves in Both Directions

  • Observe repeating patterns and turn them into deterministic components
  • Observe underperforming code and replace with probabilistic components
  • Runtime observability becomes as important as thorough testing
  • Make sure your architecture allows you to easily move the line


Moving the Line Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(19) Publish What You Have Stabilized

  • Once something is repeatable, it becomes a new official process
    • Turn repeated patterns into repeatable patterns
  • An API or a declared workflow gives consumers a capability and a contract
    • A skill gives them a capability, with no promise about where on the range it sits
  • Skills are good starting points but not very good as stable components


Moving the Line Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(20) Publishing Makes the Line Harder to Move

  • A published contract is a commitment not to change
  • Any changes in behavior become breaking changes
  • Components need versioning, deprecation, and backwards-compatible evolution
    • Consumers turn a decision into a commitment
  • The GenAI divide is a new driver of an old architectural problem

(22) As Little Runtime AI As Possible

  • GenAI is just another way to get something done
  • Make deliberate choices when to use GenAI
  • Keep the line between the two realms visible and movable
